source_text:
Πρόβατον ἤκουσεν· Ὡς γὰρ πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος
αὐτὸν ἄφωνος· πρόβατον ἤκουσεν διὰ τὴν σφαγὴν καὶ διὰ τὴν τῶν ἁγίων μελῶν αὐτοῦ μετάλημψιν καὶ τὴν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ ἁγίου αἵματος αὐτοῦ σφραγίδος ἀθάνατον αὐτοῦ φυλακήν. Ποιμὴν ἤκουσεν· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, ἐπειδὴ τὰ πεπλανημένα πρόβατα ἐπέστρεψεν καὶ τὸν ἀντίδικον ἡμῶν λέοντα τῇ βακτηρίᾳ τοῦ σταυροῦ ἀπέκτεινεν. Μαργαρίτης ἤκουσεν διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν ὥσπερ μαργαρίτην ἐν μύακι ἀνὰ μέσον δύο πτυχῶν σώματος καὶ ψυχῆς παρθενικῆς ἄνευ σπορᾶς ἀνδρὸς γεγεννῆσθαι ἢ διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν κόσμιον ψυχῆς ἢ διὰ τὸ πολυφεγγὲς αὐτοῦ καὶ καθαρὸν καὶ πανταχόθεν τῇ αἴγλῃ τῆς θεότητος ἐξάστραπτον. Φῶς ἤκουσεν, ἦν γὰρ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν, ὃ φωτίζει πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐρχόμενον εἰς τὸν κόσμον, ἐπειδὴ τὴν ζοφερὰν πλάνην τῆς παλαιᾶς σκοτομήνης ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας ἡμῶν ἀπήλασεν καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ ἡγεμονικοῦ ἡμῶν νοῦ διήνοιξεν, ἵνα ἴδωμεν ἀληθῶς οἷς προσεκυνοῦμεν τὸ πρίν, ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶ θεοί, ἀλλ' ἔργα χειρῶν ἀνθρώπων, λίθοι καὶ ξύλα. Λίθος ἀκρογωνιαῖος ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδὴ τοὺς δύο λαοὺς καθάπερ δύο τοίχους τῇ πίστει οἰκοδομήσας ἐπάνω αὐτῶν ἐπίκειται εἰς μίαν ἁρμογὴν σωτηρίας συνάγων. Ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης ἤκουσεν διὰ τὸ φωτεινὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ θερμόν –οὐκ ἔστιν γὰρ ὃς ἀποκρυβήσεται τὴν θέρμην αὐτοῦ, καὶ διὰ τὸ δωδεκάκτινον φῶς τῶν ἀποστόλων. Κόκκος σινάπεως ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδὴ σμικρύνει ἑαυτὸν καὶ συγκαταβαίνει ταῖς ἕξεσιν ἡμῶν παρὰ τὰς ἀρχὰς τῆς πίστεως, εἶθ' ὁπόταν εἰς τοὺς αὔλακας τῆς ψυχῆς ἡμῶν ἐμφωλεύσας εἰς βάθος διαχυθῇ, εἰς ὕψος οὐρανομῆκες ἐπαιρόμενος πρὸς εὐσέβειαν καὶ φρόνησιν ἀναθερμαίνεται. Σκώληξ ἤκουσεν· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι σκώληξ καὶ οὐκ ἄνθρωπος, διὰ τὸ τὴν ἐξαστράπτουσαν θεότητα καθάπερ ἄγκιστρον τῷ σκώληκι τοῦ σώματος κρύψαντα αὐτὸν εἰς τόνδε τὸν βυθὸν τοῦ βίου χαλάσαντα καὶ ὥσπερ καλὸν ἁλιέα ἀνασπάσαντα πληρῶσαι τὸ γεγραμμένον· Ἄξεις δράκοντα ἐν ἀγκίστρῳ. Ἄνθρωπος ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδὴ σῶμα ἐφόρησεν οὐκ ἐξ ἡδονῆς καὶ ὕπνου συνεστώς, ἀλλ' ἐκ παρθένου καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου γεγονώς. Ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ ἕκαστος ἡμῶν, ἀγαπητοί, ἐκδέχεται καὶ τὴν τῶν πατέρων μελίρρυτον διδασκαλίαν, ἐνταῦθα τὸ βαλάντιον ἡμῶν τῶν λόγων σφραγισώμεθα ἁγίῳ πνεύματι, ἵνα αὐτοὶ ἐλθόντες ἐκ τῆς μελισταγοῦς σοφίας τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τὰς δεξαμενὰς τῶν καρδιῶν ἡμῶν πληρώσωσιν, καὶ πολὺν τὸν καρπὸν τῆς εὐσεβείας ἕκαστος ὑμῶν βλαστήσῃ καὶ ὁ μὲν ποιήσῃ τριάκοντα, ὁ δὲ ἑξήκοντα, ὁ δὲ ἑκατὸν τὸν στέφανον τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, μεθ' οὗ τῷ πατρὶ δόξα, τιμή, κράτος ἅμα τῷ ἁγίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ πνεύματι, νῦν καὶ εἰς τοὺς σύμπαντας αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The Names of Christ Concluded and the Homily Sealed
orientation: Amphilochius is finishing his list of Christ's names and works, then closing the homily by deferring to the fathers' teaching and blessing the congregation.
pass_a_gloss: Sheep he heard; For as a sheep to slaughter he was led and as a lamb before the [one] shearing it voiceless; sheep he heard because of the slaughter and because of the of the holy members of him participation and the from the of the holy blood of him seal immortal of him protection. Shepherd he heard; I for am the shepherd the good, since the wandering sheep he turned back and the adversary of us lion with the staff of the cross he killed. Pearl he heard because of the him like a pearl in a mussel in [the] middle of two folds of body and of soul of a virgin without seed of a man to have been born or because of the to be him an ornament of soul or because of the much-shining of him and pure and from everywhere with the radiance of the divinity flashing like lightning. Light he heard, for he was the light the true, which enlightens every man coming into the world, since the dark error of the old darkness from the mind of us he drove away and the eyes of the ruling [part] of us mind he opened, in order that we might see truly [the things] to which we used to worship formerly, that not they are gods, but works of hands of men, stones and pieces of wood. Stone cornerstone he heard, since the two peoples just as two walls with the faith having built upon them he lies upon [them] into one joining of salvation bringing together. Sun of righteousness he heard because of the bright of him and hot —not there is [one] who will be hidden from the heat of him, and because of the twelve-rayed light of the apostles. Grain of mustard he heard, since he makes small himself and comes down to the conditions of us beyond the beginnings of the faith, then whenever into the furrows of the soul of us having nestled into depth he is spread, into height heaven-tall being lifted up toward piety and prudence he is warmed. Worm he heard; I for am a worm and not a man, because of the the flashing like lightning divinity just as a hook with the worm of the body having hidden himself into this the depth of the life having let down and just as a good fisherman having drawn up to fulfill the [thing] having been written; You will bring a dragon with a hook. Man he heard, since a body he wore not from pleasure and sleep having been composed, but from a virgin and [the] Spirit Holy having been born. But since each of us, beloved, awaits also the of the fathers honey-flowing teaching, here the purse of us of the words let us seal with [the] Holy Spirit, in order that they having come from the honey-dripping wisdom of the Lord of us Jesus Christ the cisterns of the hearts of us may fill, and much the fruit of piety each of you may sprout and the one may make thirty, the other sixty, the other a hundred the crown of the angels, in Christ Jesus the Lord of us, with whom to the Father glory, honor, might together with the Holy and life-giving Spirit, now and into the all ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.why: The aorist passive of ἀκούω with a predicate nominative means 'he was called' or 'he heard himself called'; 'was called' preserves the passive force and the repeated formula of the section.

choices.english: before the one shearing it voiceless
choices.why: The participle κείραντος is aorist active, 'the one shearing'; 'voiceless' renders ἄφωνος as a predicate adjective, keeping the word order and the scriptural echo.

choices.english: with the staff of the cross
choices.why: βακτηρία is a staff or rod; the metaphor of the cross as a shepherd's staff is central to the image of Christ the shepherd killing the lion.
rejected: with the club of the cross
with the rod of the cross

choices.term: ἐν μύακι ἀνὰ μέσον δύο πτυχῶν σώματος καὶ ψυχῆς παρθενικῆς
choices.english: in an oyster between two folds of a virginal body and soul
choices.why: The pearl-in-oyster image is explicit; πτυχῶν means 'folds' or 'layers', and παρθενικῆς modifies both body and soul, so 'of a virginal body and soul' keeps the genitive scope.
rejected: in a shell between two folds of virgin body and soul
in an oyster amid two folds, of body and of virgin soul

choices.why: ἐπίκειται is present middle/passive of ἐπίκειμαι, 'lies upon'; the cornerstone rests on the two walls, and the present tense conveys the ongoing state.

choices.term: τὸ βαλάντιον ἡμῶν τῶν λόγων σφραγισώμεθα
choices.english: let us seal our purse of words
choices.why: βαλάντιον is a money-pouch or purse; the metaphor of sealing a purse of words with the Spirit is vivid and should be kept literal.
rejected: let us seal our treasury of words

pass_b_english: He was called sheep: For he was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before the one shearing it, voiceless (Isaiah 53:7). He was called sheep because of the slaughter, and because of the partaking of his holy members, and because of the immortal protection that comes from the seal of his holy blood. He was called shepherd: For I am the good shepherd (John 10:11), because he turned back the wandering sheep and killed our adversary the lion with the staff of the cross. He was called pearl because he was born like a pearl in an oyster, between two folds of a virginal body and soul, without the seed of a man—or because he is the adornment of the soul, or because of his many-rayed and pure brightness, flashing out on every side with the radiance of divinity. He was called light: for he was the true light, which enlightens every person coming into the world (John 1:9), because he drove the dark error of the old moonless night from our understanding and opened the eyes of our governing mind, so that we might truly see that the things we formerly worshiped are not gods but works of human hands, stones and wood. He was called cornerstone, because he built up the two peoples like two walls by faith and lies upon them, joining them into one fitting of salvation. He was called sun of righteousness because of his brightness and warmth—for there is no one who will hide from his heat—and because of the twelve-rayed light of the apostles. He was called mustard seed, because he makes himself small and comes down to our condition at the beginnings of faith; then, when he has burrowed into the furrows of our soul and spread into its depths, he is lifted up to a height reaching heaven and grows warm toward piety and wisdom. He was called worm: For I am a worm and not a man (Psalm 22:6, LXX 21:7), because he hid his flashing divinity like a hook in the worm of his body, let himself down into this deep of life, and like a good fisherman drew up, to fulfill what is written: You will draw the dragon with a hook (Job 41:1, LXX 40:25). He was called man, because he wore a body that came not from pleasure and sleep but from a virgin and the Holy Spirit. But since each of us, beloved, is waiting also for the honey-flowing teaching of the fathers, let us seal our purse of words here with the Holy Spirit, so that when they come from the honey-dripping wisdom of our Lord Jesus Christ they may fill the cisterns of our hearts, and each of you may sprout much fruit of piety—one may bear thirty, another sixty, another the hundredfold crown of the angels—in Christ Jesus our Lord, with whom to the Father be glory, honor, and might, together with the Holy and life-giving Spirit, now and to all the ages of ages. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: lies upon them, joining them into one fitting of salvation
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐπάνω αὐτῶν ἐπίκειται εἰς μίαν ἁρμογὴν σωτηρίας συνάγων
last_rejected.why: Source says Christ rests 'upon them' (the two walls), not 'lies upon them'; 'fitting' is odd for 'joining/bond'
last_rejected.fix: rests upon them, joining them into one bond of salvation
last_rejected.ruling: 'lies upon' = normal English for ἐπίκειται; 'fitting' = ἁρμογὴν, a joint/bond, within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: He was called sheep: For he was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before the one shearing it, voiceless (Isaiah 53:7).
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὡς γὰρ πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος
last_rejected.why: The citation Isaiah 53:7 is wrong; this matches Acts 8:32 (quoting Isaiah) or could be left uncited, but the exact wording with "shearing" follows Acts 8:32.
last_rejected.fix: He was called sheep: For he was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before the one shearing it, voiceless (Acts 8:32).
last_rejected.ruling: ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος matches Isaiah 53:7 LXX; Acts 8:32 quotes the same verse.

last_rejected.quote: because he built up the two peoples like two walls by faith and lies upon them
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐπειδὴ τοὺς δύο λαοὺς καθάπερ δύο τοίχους τῇ πίστει οἰκοδομήσας ἐπάνω αὐτῶν ἐπίκειται
last_rejected.why: "lies upon them" misreads ἐπίκειται as "lies"; it means "rests upon/is laid upon" them as cornerstone.
last_rejected.fix: because he built up the two peoples like two walls by faith and rests upon them, joining them into one fitting of salvation.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπίκειται means 'lies/rests upon'; 'lies upon them' is correct, not a mistranslation.

last_rejected.quote: and like a good fisherman drew up, to fulfill what is written: You will draw the dragon with a hook
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ ὥσπερ καλὸν ἁλιέα ἀνασπάσαντα πληρῶσαι τὸ γεγραμμένον· Ἄξεις δράκοντα ἐν ἀγκίστρῳ
last_rejected.why: "drew up" lacks object; ἀνασπάσαντα takes implicit object (the dragon). "You will draw" should be "You will lead/drag" for Ἄξεις.
last_rejected.fix: and like a good fisherman drew up the dragon, to fulfill what is written: You will lead the dragon with a hook.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνασπάσαντα implies object from context; Ἄξεις can mean 'draw'; both renderings are acceptable.
